title: My Weekly Routine at WKU
writingModel: My Weekly Routine at WKU — by Kamila Seitkali

I am a second-year Linguistics student at WKU. My week is busy, but I have a routine that helps me manage everything without feeling stressed. I usually wake up at 7:15 and spend the first ten minutes planning my day in a small notebook. I always eat breakfast — I find that I concentrate much better when I have something to eat in the morning.

My weekdays follow a similar pattern. I have lectures from 8:00 to 14:00, with short breaks in between. During breaks, I quickly review my notes or chat with classmates in the corridor. I never use my phone during lectures — I put it on silent and focus completely on what the professor is saying. After lunch, I usually spend one or two hours in the library completing assignments or reading ahead for the next class.

Three times a week — on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday — I go for a short run after classes. It takes about twenty-five minutes and helps me clear my head after a long day of studying. I find it quite difficult to motivate myself on cold mornings, but I always feel better afterwards. On Tuesdays and Thursdays, I attend the English Conversation Club at 5 p.m. — it meets for ninety minutes and we practise speaking on different topics.

My evenings are quieter. I usually cook a simple dinner — something like pasta or fried rice — and eat while watching a short documentary in English. I find this a very efficient way to practise the language without feeling like I am "studying". I rarely go to bed later than 11 p.m. during the week because I know that sleep affects my concentration the next day.

Weekends are completely different. I sleep longer, call my family in Almaty, and meet friends at a café in the afternoon. I do some studying on Sunday — usually preparing for the week ahead — but I always leave time for things I enjoy. I sometimes visit a museum or art gallery with my roommate Zarina, and we occasionally cook a big meal together in the evening.

Looking back at my routine, I think the most important thing I have learned at university is that small, consistent habits are more powerful than occasional bursts of hard work. I do not always study brilliantly, and I do not always run quickly or cook well. But I always show up, every single day, and that is what makes the difference.
